claims.statement: Rodent intranasal biodistribution data alone are insufficient to predict reproducible intact-EV CNS exposure in larger species without matching intact-EV assays and bridging controls.
claims.rationale: Cross-species biodistribution literature and characterization guidance indicate limited translatability absent orthogonal intact-EV analytics and controlled bridging studies.

claims.statement: Rodent intranasal MSC-derived EVs show reproducible benefit in injury models and justify further candidate-defining and translational studies but do not by themselves demonstrate intact-EV CNS exposure in larger species.

claims.statement: Current materials do not demonstrate characterized source-cell MCB/WCB or scalable, reproducible production sufficient to support advancing a specific intranasal formulation.
claims.rationale: No MCB/WCB, validated scale-up or reproducibility data provided; MISEV recommends defined production controls and reporting.

claims.statement: An orthogonal QC panel (particles, protein, lipid markers per MISEV), validated intact-EV assays (LLOQ, specificity, precision), and stability-indicating, mechanism-linked potency assays are required before formulation advancement.
claims.rationale: MISEV2023 consensus supports orthogonal characterization and transparent release/assay criteria to de-risk identity and potency claims.

claims.statement: Intranasal CNS delivery of EVs does not reliably translate across species: one macaque study found negligible brain uptake and no reliable CSF signal after intranasal administration of Expi293F-derived EVs.
claims.rationale: This directly limits extrapolation from rodent localization studies; differences in EV source, formulation, labeling, dosing, and administration remain possible explanations.

evidence.title: Intranasal MSC-derived A1-exosomes ease inflammation, and prevent abnormal neurogenesis and memory dysfunction after status epilepticus
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: after status epilepticus in young mice, intranasally administered human MSC-derived EVs were reported in the hippocampus and were associated with reduced neuronal loss and inflammation and preservation of neurogenesis and cognitive or memory outcomes versus vehicle.

evidence.title: Extracellular vesicles from immortalized mesenchymal stromal cells protect against neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain injury
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: repeated intranasal EV administration after hypoxic-ischemic injury reduced brain tissue atrophy in neonatal mice; EVs from a clonal immortalized MSC line and primary MSCs showed comparable effects. The study frames source-cell consistency and scale as translational considerations.

evidence.title: Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles (MISEV2023): From basic to advanced approaches
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: the ISEV consensus identifies continuing challenges in EV nomenclature, separation from non-vesicular particles, characterization, functional studies, production reporting, and in-vivo evaluation; it recommends transparent, orthogonal characterization and appropriate controls.

evidence.title: Pharmacokinetics and biodistribution of extracellular vesicles administered intravenously and intranasally to Macaca nemestrina
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: reporter-labeled Expi293F-derived EVs administered intranasally to macaques were not reliably detected above background in CSF, showed negligible brain uptake, and were strongly retained in nasal lavage. EV source, formulation, labeling, administration, and species may affect generalizability.

hypotheses.statement: Advancing an intranasal formulation into high-confidence delivery and cross-species PK/PD testing requires completion of a defined CMC/analytics/formulation compatibility gating package.
hypotheses.rationale: To ensure observed in vivo signal is attributable to intact EV and is reproducible across lots/species, the program must meet orthogonal analytical and process reproducibility criteria before bridging studies.
hypotheses.test_plan: Stage 1 completion criteria: MCB/WCB produced; orthogonal QC panel defined and assays fit-for-purpose validated (LLOQ, specificity, precision); stability-indicating potency assay correlated to an in vivo PD endpoint; reproducible release/stability/potency across ≥3 GMP-like batches; formulation/device compatibility with intact-EV recovery demonstrated ex vivo and in vivo (controls included).

risks.title: Cross-species translation uncertainty for intranasal intact-EV CNS exposure
risks.description: Rodent intranasal biodistribution may not predict large-species/NHP CNS exposure for intact EV; device and formulation interactions may differ by species.
risks.mitigation: Require ex vivo nasal recovery and rodent intact-EV-specific PK with controls prior to any large-species study; predefine bridging acceptance criteria and include disrupted-EV and free-label controls in all in vivo studies.

risks.title: Insufficient CMC/analytics to establish intact-EV identity, potency, and lot-to-lot reproducibility
risks.description: Lack of MCB/WCB, orthogonal QC, validated potency/stability assays, and scale-up reproducibility may produce misleading in vitro and in vivo results and block regulatory acceptance.
risks.mitigation: Execute Stage 1 actions: generate MCB/WCB, define/validate orthogonal assays, produce representative GMP-like batches, and document stability/potency reproducibility. Escalate assay development resourcing if timelines slip.

risks.title: Model generalizability from injury models to cognition/aging endpoints
risks.description: Efficacy evidence is from acute/injury rodent models; relevance to cognition/aging indications is unproven.
risks.mitigation: Defer indication-specific efficacy studies until biodistribution/PD linkage is demonstrated; design follow-on efficacy models that reflect intended clinical endpoints.

claims.statement: Intranasally administered EV preparations have been reported to reach CNS compartments or CNS-resident cells in multiple mouse studies.
Intranasal EV treatment was associated with improved inflammatory, histologic, or functional outcomes in several rodent CNS injury or disease models.

A clonal immortalized MSC source produced EVs with activity comparable to primary MSC-EVs in one neonatal mouse hypoxic-ischemic injury study, suggesting a testable route to reduce source heterogeneity during scale-up.

EV development requires controlled production, separation, identity and purity characterization, functional testing, and transparent reporting because EV preparations are heterogeneous and may contain non-vesicular co-isolates.

critique.strongestObjection: Authorization would be premature if interpreted as approval of a fixed product or efficacy program: the local evidence supports a gated learning package, not a final source-cell, purification process, dose, potency specification, exposure threshold, or clinical indication.
assumptionsChallenged: The evidence does not compare candidate-like SGL-001 formulations under a common manufacturing and analytical framework.
Rodent biological activity does not establish clinically relevant CNS exposure or human efficacy.
The macaque result materially weakens unqualified extrapolation of rodent intranasal delivery findings.
translationalConcerns: The hypothesis is plausible enough to test but remains highly sensitive to EV source, preparation purity, label artifacts, disease-model permeability, nasal retention, dose normalization, and cross-species anatomy. Rodent efficacy cannot establish that SGL-001 reaches a clinically relevant human CNS compartment or will benefit patients.
experimentalConfounders: Demonstrate that measured CNS signal represents intact candidate-associated EV exposure rather than free label, co-isolates, or secondary biological effects.
Define product identity, purity, dose units, stability, and a mechanism-relevant potency assay before interpreting efficacy reproducibility.
Use a staged translational plan because the macaque biodistribution result conflicts with assuming that rodent intranasal brain uptake will generalize to humans.
falsificationConditions: Compare a characterized candidate formulation with vehicle, free-label, and disrupted-EV controls; quantify intact-EV-associated exposure across CNS, nasal, pulmonary, and systemic compartments over time; pair exposure with a predefined neuroregeneration-relevant pharmacodynamic assay, then evaluate cognitive function in an aging-relevant model only if prospectively defined exposure, reproducibility, and safety criteria are met.

recentReviews.matter_question: What minimum source-cell, EV identity, cargo, and release definition is required before SGL-001 can be treated as a candidate-like product?
recentReviews.strongest_case_for: Preclinical rodent studies show repeated intranasal MSC-derived EV dosing can reduce injury-associated pathology and functional deficits (Hermann neonatal HI plus earlier intranasal EV studies), and the ISEV/MISEV2023 consensus provides a clear set of requirements for orthogonal EV characterization, functional controls, and reporting that define what candidate-level CMC and quality work should cover.
recentReviews.strongest_case_against: The proposed gate and minimum-definition plan assumes that (a) intranasal intact‑EV CNS delivery observed in rodents will be predictive for larger species/humans and (b) a candidate-like product can be meaningfully specified (release limits, potency assay) prior to selecting therapeutic cargo/mechanism. The primary objection is that cross‑species delivery uncertainty and the unspecified cargo/potency approach make the recommended candidate-definition and go/no‑go criteria premature and potentially uninformative for translational decision‑making.
recentReviews.determination: Approve a mandatory two-stage candidate-definition and biodistribution gate before treating SGL-001 as a candidate-like product: (1) finalize source-cell choice and establish MCB/WCB; define orthogonal identity/purity QC panel and draft release specifications; develop a fit-for-purpose potency assay concept in parallel with small-scale process development; (2) execute a controlled biodistribution/PK/PD bridging package (rodent plus a large species, preferably NHP) that includes intact‑EV quantitative analytics with vehicle, free‑label, and disrupted‑EV controls, predefined acceptance criteria for CNS exposure and non-vesicular signal, and basic safety/tolerability. Require validated analytics that distinguish intact EV signal from label artifacts and demonstrate PK→PD linkage in the large species before advancement. Major therapeutic advancement decisions require human approval and should remain pending.

developmentGates.name: Intranasal Delivery

Current materials do not demonstrate characterized source-cell MCB/WCB or scalable, reproducible production sufficient to support advancing a specific intranasal formulation.
developmentGates.next_action: Require ex vivo nasal recovery and rodent intact-EV-specific PK with controls prior to any large-species study; predefine bridging acceptance criteria and include disrupted-EV and free-label controls in all in vivo studies.

candidates.name: Native MSC-EV secretome cargo
candidates.source: MSC-derived small extracellular vesicles; final source-cell strategy not selected
candidates.mechanism: Multi-component paracrine signaling intended to support neuroregeneration-relevant and inflammation-modulating activity; active components remain undefined.
candidates.rationale: This is the operator-selected program focus because it preserves the multi-component EV thesis and has relevant rodent activity, while MISEV2023 highlights the characterization burden.
candidates.uncertainty: The active cargo components, potency mechanism, source-cell dependence, and relevance to cognition or aging are not established.

candidates.name: Curcumin-loaded EV benchmark
candidates.source: Exogenous curcumin loaded into an exosome preparation
candidates.mechanism: Delivery of an anti-inflammatory small-molecule payload using EVs as a carrier.
candidates.rationale: The current evidence is more cargo-specific than for the native secretome, making this an informative benchmark rather than the selected product focus.
candidates.uncertainty: The cited mouse models and loaded payload do not establish relevance to an unengineered SGL-001 product or human cognitive benefit.

candidates.name: STAT3-inhibitor-loaded EV benchmark
candidates.source: Exogenous STAT3 inhibitor loaded into an exosome preparation
candidates.mechanism: EV-mediated delivery of a pathway-directed inhibitor in a model-specific CNS context.
candidates.rationale: This is retained as a pathway-directed delivery benchmark, not as the current SGL-001 development focus.
candidates.uncertainty: Model-specific activity, payload safety, and relevance to cognition or aging remain unresolved.

candidates.name: miR-21
candidates.mechanism: Anti-apoptotic, pro-angiogenic, pro-survival — the single most consistently reported MSC-EV miRNA across regenerative contexts.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Among the most abundant miRNAs in MSC-EV cargo generally, not a marker specific to regenerative signaling — an 'enrichment' claim needs a naive-EV or non-MSC-EV control to mean anything.
candidates.sourceCitation: Zhu et al., 2017, J Cell Mol Med (MSC-EV miR-21, PTEN/PI3K-Akt cardioprotection)

candidates.name: miR-126
candidates.mechanism: Pro-angiogenic, supports endothelial barrier integrity.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Foundational mechanistic work (Fish et al.) is endothelial-cell biology, not MSC-EV-specific — the MSC-EV cargo literature builds on it rather than originating it.
candidates.sourceCitation: Fish et al., 2008, Dev Cell (foundational, non-MSC); Tao et al., 2017, Theranostics (BMSC-exosome miR-126-3p, diabetic wound)

candidates.name: miR-132
candidates.mechanism: Pro-angiogenic; also reported for neurite outgrowth in CNS contexts.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: RASA1 is a RasGAP acting on Ras/MAPK signaling, not strictly the PI3K-Akt axis — grouped here with the closest recurring node, not a clean fit.
candidates.sourceCitation: Katare et al., 2014, Circ Res (stem-cell-derived exosomal miR-132, cardiac angiogenesis)

candidates.name: miR-146a
candidates.mechanism: Canonically anti-inflammatory via NF-κB dampening, but direction of net effect on inflammation and downstream tissue outcome varies by model and dose.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Reversal is dose- and context-dependent — the same miR-146a delivery has been reported anti-inflammatory in some macrophage/inflammation models and associated with different, sometimes opposing, downstream effects in others. Do not treat 'anti-inflammatory' as a fixed label for this miRNA without checking the specific model.
candidates.sourceCitation: Multiple independent reports of direction-of-effect divergence; representative primary sources need direct verification before citing a specific reversal claim externally.

candidates.name: miR-125b
candidates.mechanism: Regulates apoptosis and proliferation via p53 pathway components; reported both pro-survival (protective, anti-apoptotic) and growth-suppressive depending on target-cell context.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: One of the clearer documented direction-of-effect reversals in this cargo set — p53-axis regulation by miR-125b is well known in the oncology literature to flip between tumor-suppressive and oncogenic roles depending on cell type, and MSC-EV regenerative contexts inherit that same ambiguity rather than resolving it.
candidates.sourceCitation: p53/BAK1 targeting is well established generally; the specific MSC-EV regenerative-context reversal citations need direct verification before external use.

candidates.name: miR-29
candidates.mechanism: Anti-fibrotic — suppresses collagen deposition and extracellular-matrix accumulation; the clearest TGF-β/SMAD-axis counterweight in this cargo set.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Foundational target validation (van Rooij et al.) is direct cardiac-tissue miRNA biology, not MSC-EV cargo transfer specifically — treat as the mechanistic basis the MSC-EV literature draws on.
candidates.sourceCitation: van Rooij et al., 2008, PNAS (miR-29 and cardiac fibrosis via collagen targeting — foundational, non-MSC)

candidates.name: let-7
candidates.mechanism: Differentiation-promoting, anti-proliferative tumor-suppressor family; regulates the stemness-to-senescence transition broadly across tissues.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Family-level entry covering multiple mature let-7 isoforms with overlapping but not identical targets. The documented direction-of-effect reversal is specific to the let-7b isoform (pro- vs. anti-angiogenic reported in different studies) — do not assume it generalizes to the whole family.
candidates.sourceCitation: Roush & Slack, 2008, Trends Cell Biol (let-7 family review, foundational, non-MSC); let-7b-specific reversal citations need direct verification.

candidates.name: miR-210
candidates.mechanism: The archetypal 'hypoxamir' — induced under hypoxic preconditioning, pro-angiogenic and pro-survival under ischemic conditions.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Effect and abundance are strongly dependent on whether the parental MSCs were hypoxia-preconditioned before EV harvest — normoxic-culture MSC-EVs carry substantially less miR-210, and results don't transfer across culture conditions.
candidates.sourceCitation: Chan & Loscalzo, 2010, Cell Cycle (miR-210 as 'hypoxamir', foundational review, non-MSC-specific)

candidates.name: miR-221/222
candidates.mechanism: Promotes proliferation and reduces apoptosis via p27/p57 suppression; also reported to modulate angiogenesis.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Foundational target-validation work is oncology-derived (proliferation control), not MSC-EV-specific — the regenerative-context application is a later extension.
candidates.sourceCitation: le Sage et al., 2007, EMBO J (miR-221/222 regulation of p27Kip1 — foundational, non-MSC)

candidates.name: miR-133b
candidates.mechanism: Promotes neurite outgrowth and neural plasticity; anti-fibrotic via CTGF suppression.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: The strongest single MSC-EV in-vivo functional-transfer demonstration in this cargo set (rat stroke model, direct EV-mediated transfer shown), which is why it's a common reference point in the stoichiometry debate about whether EV miRNA cargo can be functionally meaningful at reported copy numbers.
candidates.sourceCitation: Xin et al., 2013, Stem Cells (MSC-exosome miR-133b transfer, neural plasticity and functional recovery after stroke in rats)

candidates.name: miR-17-92
candidates.mechanism: Cluster-level pro-angiogenic and pro-neurogenic effect via suppression of anti-angiogenic targets (CTGF, TSP1) alongside direct PTEN suppression.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Cluster of six co-transcribed miRNAs (17, 18a, 19a, 19b, 20a, 92a) reported as a unit in most MSC-EV work — individual-member contributions are not always separated. The documented direction-of-effect reversal in this cargo set is specific to the miR-92a member, not the cluster as a whole.
candidates.sourceCitation: Xin et al., 2017, Stem Cells (MSC-exosome miR-17-92 cluster enrichment, neuroplasticity and functional recovery after stroke in rats)

candidates.name: miR-486-5p
candidates.mechanism: Muscle-enriched miRNA; promotes myoblast survival/regeneration and is separately reported cardioprotective via the same PTEN axis.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Foundational work establishes this as a muscle-tissue-intrinsic miRNA (myomiR), not an MSC-EV discovery — MSC-EV cargo studies build on that baseline biology.
candidates.sourceCitation: Small et al., 2010, PNAS (miR-486 regulation of PI3K/Akt signaling via PTEN, muscle-enriched — foundational, non-MSC)

candidates.name: miR-22-3p
candidates.mechanism: Anti-apoptotic and anti-fibrotic in cardiac contexts, reported to act partly through HMGB1-mediated inflammatory signaling suppression.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Lower citation confidence than most entries in this file — the foundational cardiac-hypertrophy role of miR-22 is well established, but the specific MSC-EV cargo delivery mechanism is a thinner literature and needs direct verification before use.
candidates.sourceCitation: Huang et al., 2013, Circ Res (miR-22 and cardiac hypertrophy — foundational, non-MSC-EV-specific; MSC-EV-specific citation not confidently recalled)

candidates.name: miR-100-5p
candidates.mechanism: Induces autophagy via mTOR suppression; reported neuroprotective and (separately, in tumor angiogenesis literature) anti-angiogenic depending on context.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: The anti-angiogenic mTOR-suppression literature for this miRNA is largely tumor-biology work, not regenerative-medicine work — the neuroprotective/autophagy framing used here is the regenerative-context reading, and the two literatures shouldn't be conflated.
candidates.sourceCitation: Grundmann et al., 2011, Circulation (miR-100 regulation of neovascularization via mTOR suppression — foundational, non-MSC-EV-specific)

candidates.name: miR-181
candidates.mechanism: Family-level entry (181a/b/c/d) — reported roles in myogenesis, immune modulation, and (miR-181c specifically) mitochondrial gene regulation.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Family members have distinct, sometimes non-overlapping target sets — treating 'miR-181' as one biological entity for scoring purposes understates real isoform-level heterogeneity. Isoform should be specified before any claim is used downstream of this record.
candidates.sourceCitation: Indrieri et al., 2020, EMBO Mol Med (miR-181a/b and mitochondrial disease models — moderate citation confidence, verify directly)

candidates.name: miR-24
candidates.mechanism: Anti-apoptotic cardioprotection via Bim suppression.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Engineered/loaded cargo — enriched via parental-cell genetic modification (GATA-4 overexpression), not representative of naive MSC-EV content. Per the literature agent's standing rule, findings here do not transfer to an unloaded/naive product without separate confirmation.
candidates.sourceCitation: Yu et al., 2015, Int J Cardiol (GATA-4-overexpressing MSC exosomes as a reservoir of anti-apoptotic miRNAs, cardioprotection)

candidates.name: miR-19a
candidates.mechanism: Anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory (macrophage polarization) cardioprotection; co-reported alongside miR-24 in the same engineered-cargo model.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Engineered/loaded cargo — same GATA-4-overexpression construct as miR-24 above. Also a native member of the miR-17-92 cluster (see that entry) — the engineered version here is deliberately enriched beyond native cluster levels, so this is not simply 'more of the same cargo.'
candidates.sourceCitation: Yu et al., 2015, Int J Cardiol (GATA-4-overexpressing MSC exosomes, miR-19a, PTEN/SOCS1, cardioprotection)

candidates.name: miR-410
candidates.mechanism: Chondroprotective, anti-catabolic in osteoarthritis models — reported to suppress Wnt-pathway-driven cartilage degradation.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Engineered/loaded cargo, and this is the lowest-confidence citation in the file — the target/pathway assignment is directionally consistent with the broader engineered-MSC-EV cartilage literature but the specific primary paper was not confidently recalled. Verify before relying on this entry for anything beyond a placeholder.
candidates.sourceCitation: Not confidently recalled — requires a direct literature search before citing; tentatively associated with engineered MSC-EV osteoarthritis chondroprotection studies.

candidates.name: miR-214-3p
candidates.mechanism: Native miR-214-3p (notably from osteoclast-derived EVs) suppresses osteoblastic bone formation via ATF4; the engineered regenerative application uses an anti-miR-214-3p construct loaded into MSC-EVs to counteract that suppression and promote osteogenesis.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'msc'.
candidates.uncertainty: Direction of effect depends entirely on whether the cargo is native miR-214-3p (bone-formation-suppressive, originally characterized in osteoclast-derived EVs, not MSC-EVs) or an engineered anti-miR-214-3p construct (bone-formation-promoting). These are opposite interventions sharing one entry — do not read 'effect' without checking which construct a given source used.
candidates.sourceCitation: Sun et al., 2016, J Extracell Vesicles / Bone Research (osteoclast-derived exosomal miR-214-3p inhibits osteoblastic bone formation via ATF4 — the suppressive/native finding this engineered application is designed to counteract)

candidates.name: miR-302
candidates.mechanism: Maintains pluripotency and promotes reprogramming efficiency by driving a rapid G1/S cell-cycle transition characteristic of pluripotent cells.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'pluripotent'.
candidates.uncertainty: The foundational literature is about the miRNA itself (transfection/expression), not EV-mediated transfer — whether ESC/iPSC-EVs carry functionally sufficient miR-302 cargo to reproduce these effects is a separate, less-established question from the direct-expression literature this citation reflects.
candidates.sourceCitation: Judson et al., 2009, Nat Biotechnol (embryonic-stem-cell-specific microRNAs, including the miR-302 cluster, promote induced pluripotency)

candidates.name: miR-371-373
candidates.mechanism: Human-ESC-specific cluster supporting proliferation and pluripotency maintenance via p21 and Hippo-pathway (LATS2) suppression.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'pluripotent'.
candidates.uncertainty: This cluster's largest, best-established literature is oncology (germ-cell-tumor biomarker), not regenerative medicine — the regenerative framing here is a minority use case within the broader miR-371-373 literature and should not be assumed to carry the same weight of evidence.
candidates.sourceCitation: Voorhoeve et al., 2006, Cell (miR-372/373 as oncogenes in testicular germ-cell tumors — the field's dominant citation for this cluster, not a regenerative-medicine paper)

candidates.name: miR-290-295
candidates.mechanism: Drives G1/S transition and self-renewal in mouse ESCs; regulates de novo DNA methylation indirectly via RBL2 suppression of DNMT3A/B.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'pluripotent'.
candidates.uncertainty: Mouse-specific cluster with no direct human ortholog — miR-371-373 is the human-ESC functional analogue, not the same sequence. Do not treat findings here as transferable to human cells without that substitution already made in the source study.
candidates.sourceCitation: Sinkkonen et al., 2008, Nat Struct Mol Biol (miR-290 cluster controls de novo DNA methylation via Rbl2/Dnmt3 in mouse ESCs)

candidates.name: miR-9-5p
candidates.mechanism: Dual/opposing roles reported in neural stem cell fate: represses TLX to promote differentiation while other reported activity supports proliferation — a feedback loop rather than a one-directional effect.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'pluripotent'.
candidates.uncertainty: Not included in this file's explicit context-dependent flag list, but the underlying biology (a feedback loop with opposing arms) is functionally similar to the flagged entries — worth treating with the same caution even though it isn't formally tagged that way here.
candidates.sourceCitation: Zhao, Sun, Li & Shi, 2009, Nat Struct Mol Biol (miR-9/TLX feedback loop in neural stem cell fate determination)

candidates.name: miR-296-5p
candidates.source: endothelial progenitor cells, tumor endothelium (adjacent literature)
candidates.mechanism: Pro-angiogenic — suppresses HGS-mediated degradation of growth factor receptors (VEGFR2, PDGFRβ), increasing their surface availability.
candidates.rationale: Imported biological-design candidate from legacy tier 'pluripotent'.
candidates.uncertainty: Most of the primary literature for this miRNA is tumor-angiogenesis research, not regenerative medicine — included here because the mechanism (angiogenic receptor recycling) is directly relevant to regenerative vascularization, but the source literature's intent was oncology, and that context should travel with any citation of it.
candidates.sourceCitation: Würdinger et al., 2008, Cancer Cell (miR-296 regulates growth-factor-receptor overexpression in angiogenic endothelial cells)

jurisdictions.privateClinicPath: COFEPRIS-authorized regenerative-medicine establishments and stem cell banks/collection centers may administer stem cell therapy under Art. 315 licensing and the 2026 reform's committee and consent requirements. Whether an acellular exosome/secretome product is administered under that same authorization in practice, or falls outside it, is unresolved — clinic-marketing sources describe exosome therapy being offered under the same facility authorization as stem cell therapy, with no regulatory differentiation found. Route note: Mexico already has an active, internationally-marketed private clinic sector for stem cell and exosome therapy, operating on facility-level COFEPRIS authorization (Aviso de Funcionamiento, Aviso de Publicidad) rather than product-level drug registration, per clinic-operator sources. The fast route mirrors that practice; the durable route is COFEPRIS product registration as a medicamento biotecnológico (Art. 222 Bis) — or asking COFEPRIS directly whether the 2026 stem-cell-establishment framework reaches an acellular product.
